rust.summary:
P2 is done, and every settle command passes, including the openpyxl exchange with its new fidelity half. The previous agent's partial work was kept after review, then fixed and finished.

Frame (`excel/carried.rs`): `SheetRows::capturing` keeps a byte-exact `WorksheetFrame` (declaration, root tag verbatim, carried items in document order, epilogue). The frame writer emits the model elements (dimension, sheetViews, cols, sheetData, mergeCells) in CT_Worksheet slot order, and an unknown child keeps its place after the preceding known slot. The Free/Shifted/Blocking classification follows design 2.4, including x14 extLst URIs. A sheet inserted into another workbook drops every child that names a relationship. Fixed: the carried tests' fixture lacked the shared strings and styles their cells index.

Layout (`excel/layout.rs`): `RowFormat` (a formatted row with no cell now survives), `ColumnFormat`, sorted non-overlapping `Columns`, merges, `Frozen` read from the first sheetView, and the `sheetFormatPr` defaults. Refusals now name the element (`Sheet1!col`). New public readers on `Sheet`: `column_width`, `default_column_width`, `row_height`, `default_row_height`, `is_row_hidden`, `is_column_hidden`, `row_style`, `column_style`, `merges`, `frozen`. Also new: `Frozen::top_left`, `DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH`, `DEFAULT_ROW_HEIGHT`.

Formulas (`formula.rs` + `formula/{lexer,reference,shape}.rs`) are as design 5.2, with `MAX_FORMULA_LENGTH` and `MAX_FORMULA_NESTING`:
- Shared groups share the master's `Arc`, and dependents seen before their master resolve at the end of the part.
- A dependent with no master is refused, naming the cell and the `si`.
- Normal formulas are interned per sheet.
- Array, data-table and dynamic-array attributes are kept.
- A dirty sheet writes one plain `<f>` per formula cell, with `ca` added for volatile formulas.
- Fixed: `<f>` attributes are now held unboxed, so each shared dependent no longer costs an allocation. A new pin proves a group costs one shape.

Shared strings: the table is rewritten over the original part bytes and `count` is removed. A package without a table gets a new one.

Names and workbook: `DefinedName` (`name`, `scope`, `formula`, `text`, `is_hidden`, `comment`), `Workbook::defined_names` and `active_tab`.
- Rename and remove rewrite the formulas that name the sheet (one rewrite per shape) and the names. Names scoped to a removed sheet go, and `localSheetId` is renumbered.
- Removal remaps activeTab/firstSheet and drops orphans by reference count over every `.rels`. Their Overrides go with them, and a pivot cache goes with its last table.
- `Workbook::move_sheet(name, to)` is added now rather than in P4.
- The workbook relationships are read once per save (the orphan walk and the rewrite reuse that read), pinned in `iobase_calls`.

Rich inline strings keep their runs while the cell still holds the text they spell. The inline capture reuses one buffer, pinned by `excel_inline_string_parse_costs_nothing_per_cell`.

Tests:
- `rich_package` / `rich_parts` / `rich_styles` / `rich_shared_strings` / `normalized` fixtures, and the closed-list pins `a_read_workbook_writes_back_what_it_read` and `an_edited_cell_changes_only_its_cell`.
- New or extended test files: layout, carried, names, formula/*, parser, sheet, shared_strings, and the workbook structural tests.
- openpyxl fidelity: openpyxl writes CF, DV, hyperlinks, an autofilter, a table, merges, a frozen pane, formulas, a defined name, rich text and styles. The crate edits one cell and saves, and openpyxl asserts every feature survived. I checked the assertions go red on broken files.

deviations: `carried::Class` has two variants beyond Free/Shifted/Blocking: `Modelled` (sheetViews) and `Regenerated` (dimension, cols, sheetData, mergeCells). They mark where the model writes its elements in document order. `WorksheetFrame` also holds `root_name` (for the end tag and the element prefix), `epilogue` and the `pane` it was read with; when that pane still matches the model's, sheetViews is copied verbatim.

Layout: `RowFormat` adds `custom_format` and `custom_height`, and `ColumnFormat` adds `custom_width` and `phonetic`, so they are written back. Merges are a `Vec<CellRange>`, not a `Merges` type. Refusal paths name the element (for example `Sheet1!col`), and a row attribute refusal names the row's cell.

`CellExtra::inline_runs` is `Option<Arc<RichInline{text, runs}>>`, not `Arc<[u8]>`. The runs are written back only while the cell still holds the text they spell, because `CellMut`'s DerefMut can replace the value. This mirrors the design's shared_string text guard.
The parser holds `FormulaAttributes` unboxed in `RawFormula`. Only `CellExtra::formula` boxes them, which removes one allocation per shared dependent.

The workbook's names, views, activeTab dirty flags and pivot-cache ids live in a boxed `Stated` struct. Held inline, they made clippy flag the `Held` enum in excel/media.rs (`large_enum_variant`), and media.rs is outside my file set.

Save cost: the workbook relationships part is now read once per save and its bytes reused by the rewrite. Before, a list-changing save read it twice. Pinned in `iobase_calls` with a new removal-save row whose arithmetic is stated.

`Workbook::move_sheet(name, to)` was brought forward from P4 because it was cheap here. activeTab follows the moved sheet, firstSheet stays, `localSheetId` is recomputed from the keys, and no formula is rewritten (3D spans keep their text, as in Excel).

Additional public items not listed in the design: `Frozen::top_left`, `DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH`, `DEFAULT_ROW_HEIGHT`, `MAX_FORMULA_LENGTH`, `MAX_FORMULA_NESTING`, `DefinedName::text`, and on `Sheet`: `default_column_width`, `default_row_height`, `is_column_hidden`, `row_style`, `column_style`.

The sheet-name quoting rule is pinned through the public entry API (`rust/tests/excel/formula/reference.rs`). The earlier `formula::reference::internals` forwarder is removed because rustfmt and `generate_internals.py` order `excel::formula::internals` and `excel::formula::reference::internals` differently. The two tools could never both pass.
In the carried pin, `set_cell` replaces the cell's style, which is existing `set_cell` behaviour. The expectation was corrected; no code changed.

Formula `volatile` uses the six-name stub (NOW, TODAY, RAND, RANDBETWEEN, OFFSET, INDIRECT). The `_xlfn` table in formula.rs lists 31 later functions. Unknown functions are not yet a `held` reason; the full registry is P5.
open: P4: rename and remove rewrite only cell formulas and defined names. Carried references are not rewritten yet and go stale after a rename or removal: hyperlink `@location`, chart `c:f`, CF/DV formulas, sparkline `xm:f`, pivot cache `worksheetSource@sheet`, table and autoFilter refs. The adjuster and the blocking-element refusals are P4, and so is `Sheet::insert_rows`/`remove_rows` moving to `Workbook`.
P4: `set_frozen` exists only through `yggdryl::internals::excel_layout::set_frozen`. The public layout setters (`set_frozen`, `set_column_width`, `set_row_height`, merge/unmerge, hide) are P4.
P5: the function registry and the unknown-function `held` reason. `Formula::from_entry`'s syntax check is the minimal P2 one, over the lexed tokens.

Edge case not handled: a defined name whose `localSheetId` names no tab reads as workbook-scoped (`scope() == None`) and is written as read. If a later rename or removal restates it, its `localSheetId` attribute is dropped.

P12 inventories: `.api-inventory.txt` needs `excel::{layout, names, Frozen, DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH, DEFAULT_ROW_HEIGHT, DefinedName, MAX_FORMULA_LENGTH, MAX_FORMULA_NESTING}`, `Frozen::top_left`, `DefinedName::{name, scope, formula, text, is_hidden, comment}`, `Formula::{from_entry, entry_at, is_computed}`, `Sheet::{column_width, default_column_width, row_height, default_row_height, is_row_hidden, is_column_hidden, row_style, column_style, merges, frozen}` and `Workbook::{move_sheet, active_tab, defined_names}`. Docs and skills have no entries for these yet.
P10/P11: the Python and Node bindings are still broken, as left by P1a and P1b. P2 changed no public signature they call.
Not run: the whole-workspace suite, the `--all-features` lane (CI's job), and `cargo bench`.

side.summary:
P3 UI work (Agent B) plus the change feed is done in cli/assets/excel/. I picked up the lost agent's uncommitted work, reviewed it against design §8.3–8.6, §10 and the contract addendum, and kept it. I then fixed five defects the review found. Nothing was committed. No cargo, maturin or npm build ran, and no .rs file was touched.

**New modules (kept from the previous agent, then fixed)**
- `js/status.js` (`Status`, `AGGREGATES`, `SUMMARY_DELAY`, `zoomOfSlider`, `sliderOfZoom`):
  - the mode (Ready/Enter/Edit/Point, from the editor's `mode` event);
  - a copy or loading note;
  - `Calculate (n)` from `calc.uncomputed` (click, F9, Ctrl+Alt+F9 for a full `POST calculate`);
  - `Circular References: <ref>`, which goes to the reference;
  - Average/Count/Numerical Count/Min/Max/Sum from `GET summary`, debounced 150 ms, following Excel's rule of nothing shown under two filled cells. Which ones show is chosen by right click and kept in localStorage;
  - the timezone clock, Saved/Unsaved/Read-only, and a zoom slider with 100% in its middle.
- `js/clipboard.js` (`Clipboard`, `markerOf`, `textExtent`, and now `recordCopy`, `copiedHere`):
  - Copy writes TSV and HTML from `GET export` through `navigator.clipboard.write`, falling back to the `copy`/`cut` events. The source gets a marquee.
  - Paste reads the `paste` event or `clipboard.read`. Our marker goes through the service's `paste` (cut becomes the move and pastes once); anything else goes through `pasteText`.
  - Paste Special offers all, values, formulas and formats (Ctrl+Alt+V).
  - The Format Painter is `paste` with `what: formats`: one click paints once, a double click paints until Escape.
- `js/dialogs.js` (`Dialog`, `Dialogs`, `el`, `commit`, number-code helpers):
  - the modal frame, with a focus trap, Enter for OK, and the service's refusal shown inside the dialog;
  - `confirm`, which takes over from main.js;
  - Format Cells with Number, Alignment, Font, Border and Fill tabs, sent as one `setStyle` or a `batch`;
  - Row Height and Column Width, with widths in the file's units (addendum 2);
  - Go To on Ctrl+G and F5, through `resolve`.
- `js/sync.js` (`Sync`, `CHANNEL`, `LOCK`, `WAIT`): one Web Locks leader per browser holds `GET changes?since=N&wait=25` and relays each answer over `BroadcastChannel("yggdryl-excel")`. Followers never poll. A follower with a gap reads the ring once with `wait=0`. A reset or a later generation reloads everything.

**Edits to P1/P2 files**
- `main.js`: the `app.events` bus (`workbook`, `sheet`, `edited`, `changed`, `reset`), `app.send`, `applyChanges`, and waiting for tiles when a sheet is removed.
- `api.js`: `text` and `calculate`.
- `tiles.js`: `current`, `idle`, nested holds, and stale in-flight requests.
- `editor.js`: `fillEntry` carries `ref` (addendum 6); `go` returns a reason.
- `menus.js`: Paste Special… entry. `ribbon.js`: comment updates. `index.html` and `styles.css`: status bar, dialogs, marquee.

**Contract addendum.** All seven items apply: `activeSheet` as a key; widths; `[char, offset]` fill; 0-based indices; the enum spellings; `decimals` as a ±1 delta that is never sent beside `numberFormat`; `fillEntry.ref`; the change feed.

**Fixes this session**
1. `Sync.lead` kept polling from the old generation's revision after a reset. It now restarts `since` from the tab's revision. The new unit test fails on the old loop and passes now.
2. `Status.setCalc` let a stale `circularCount` from the workbook document outlive an edit answer that lists `circular` without it.
3. The export marker carries no service identity, and `generation` is a per-process counter. Copying in one `excel serve` and pasting into another at the same generation silently ran an internal `paste` of the destination's own cells. A marker now counts as ours only if this origin's pages exported it (recorded per API in localStorage), or if it is this tab's own copy. The browser step fails on the old condition and passes now.
4. Layout: `.app` had an implicit `auto` grid column, so the status bar's min-content widened the whole page past the window, cutting the ribbon and zoom group. It is now `minmax(0, 1fr)`. A short status bar now shrinks the note first, then hides whole aggregates from the left, so Sum goes last and nothing is cut mid-number.
5. Focus and noise: cell dialogs (Format Cells, Row Height, Column Width, Go To, Paste Special) return focus to the sheet through a new `Dialog` `restore` option. A refused export toasts once instead of twice.

Scratch: `dev.py` already answered `summary`, `export`, `changes` (long poll plus `/__control` holdChanges/closed) and `calculate` over `devstore.py`. It now also tolerates aborted connections. `check.js` gained three checks: the narrow status bar, focus returning to the sheet, and the foreign-marker/other-tab paste. `unit.mjs` gained two tests (the leader loop and recorded markers).

deviations: Web Lock name is `yggdryl-changes <API pathname>` rather than bare `yggdryl-changes`, so two services under one origin at different public paths each get a leader; BroadcastChannel messages are tagged with the API base for the same reason

'Our marker' (§10) is narrowed to a marker this origin's pages exported (localStorage `yggdryl-copies`, per API base, newest 32) or this tab's own copy, and whose source cells the ring says are unchanged since the copy; otherwise the clipboard's text goes through pasteText. Adding a random per-process instance id to the marker, or making generation unique per process, would close this

Not browser-tested: Firefox and Safari clipboard paths (ClipboardItem with promise values, a paste event on a non-editable focused element, execCommand fallback timing), IME, read-only mode, pages frozen by the browser while holding the Web Lock

findings.issue: The total lexer panics on non-ASCII text after a sheet prefix. `qualified` does `self.rest(at).len() >= 5 && self.rest(at)[..5].eq_ignore_ascii_case("#REF!")`, and `[..5]` is a byte slice that splits a multi-byte character. `Formula::from_file("Sheet1!Größe", ..)` reaches it: `target_at` reads `Gr` as a column with no row and answers None, the rest is 7 bytes, and byte 5 is inside `ß`. I reproduced the same slice with rustc and it panics. `from_file` is documented as never failing and reads untrusted `<f>` and definedName text, so a file with a sheet-scoped non-ASCII name reaches the panic. The lexer tests only try `é+ü`, `'Q'` and similar, never text after `!`.
findings.fix: Use `self.rest(at).get(..5).is_some_and(|head| head.eq_ignore_ascii_case("#REF!"))`. Add lexer pins for `Sheet1!Größe`, `'Q1'!Größe*2` and `Sheet1!abcdé` under `from_file` in rust/tests/excel/formula/lexer.rs, and add them to `every_byte_of_any_text_is_kept`.

findings.issue: `cargo doc -p yggdryl --no-deps` emits 5 warnings, all from P2 lines. CI runs `cargo doc` under `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, so the Rust quality job goes red. (1) formula.rs:3, public docs link to the `pub(crate)` module `shape` (`rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links`), and the link target is also redundant. (2) layout.rs:7, public module docs link to the private module `super::carried`. (3) sheet.rs:609 and (4) sheet.rs:629, `[`DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH`](super::layout::DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH)` and the `DEFAULT_ROW_HEIGHT` twin are redundant explicit targets.
findings.fix: formula.rs:3, write the word `shape` in plain text with no link. layout.rs:7, drop the `carried` link and write `carried` as plain code text. sheet.rs:609 and sheet.rs:629, use bare `[`DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH`]` and `[`DEFAULT_ROW_HEIGHT`]`, both already imported. Re-run `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p yggdryl --no-deps`.

findings.issue: A sheet held in a different workbook keeps its carried legacy `<conditionalFormatting>` verbatim, and `rust/tests/excel/carried.rs` pins that it stays. Each `<cfRule dxfId="n">` indexes the source workbook's `dxfs`, and `hold_in` resets every other style index (cells, rows, columns) for exactly this reason but not this one. In the destination the id is either out of range or names an unrelated format. Excel repairs the first and mis-formats the second. This is new in P2, because before it the element was dropped. The fixture's `dxfId="0"` over `Workbook::new()` shows the case.
findings.fix: In `hold_in`, when `origin != workbook`, also drop the carried `conditionalFormatting` children whose rules state `dxfId`. Keep x14 conditional formats, which carry their dxf inline. Alternatively hold the element until P3 owns dxf interning and remaps the ids. Change the `a_sheet_moved_to_another_workbook...` pin to expect the drop, and add a same-workbook pin that keeps it.

findings.issue: `WorksheetFrame::detach` drops a whole carried child when its bytes contain a relationship marker, and the marker test is a substring search for ` r:`. A `<pageSetup r:id=..>` names printer settings, so paper size, orientation and scale are lost. A `<hyperlinks>` with one URL link loses every `location` link beside it. The test also misses `r:id` written after a tab or a newline, which leaves `<drawing r:id=..>` pointing at a `.rels` the new part lacks. The carried.rs pin asserts the loss of `<pageSetup` and `<hyperlinks>`, which contradicts the ordering principle that nothing Excel wrote is lost.
findings.fix: Detach at attribute granularity, by parsed attribute names in the relationships prefix or namespace. Remove only the `r:id` attribute of `pageSetup` and the like, and only the `<hyperlink>` children that carry `r:id`. Drop a whole child only when it has no meaning without its relationship (`drawing`, `legacyDrawing`, `tablePart`, `picture`). Update the pin to keep `<pageSetup paperSize orientation` and the `location` hyperlink.

findings.issue: `Stated::pivot_caches` is read once at load and never updated, and `adopt`/`mark` do not refresh `stated`. After a save that dropped a cache (with `write_into` or `rebase`), the next save's `caches_left` still counts the dropped ids. Take two caches, each with its own pivot table on its own sheet. Remove sheet A and save, then remove sheet B and save. On the second save `caches_left` is 1 (the stale id), so `<pivotCaches>` is not skipped and the file keeps an empty `<pivotCaches></pivotCaches>`, which the schema forbids (at least one entry). `a_pivot_cache_goes_with_the_last_pivot_table...` uses one cache and one save, so the sequence is untested.
findings.fix: Count the caches left from the workbook part being rewritten (its `<pivotCache>` entries not in `dropped_caches`) instead of the stale model list. Or prune `stated.pivot_caches` of the dropped ids in `mark` or `adopt` from the snapshot. Add a two-cache, two-save pin.

findings.issue: `CellExtra::formula` (array or data-table attributes) is applied to whatever cell now sits at the reference. `CellMut` documents `*cell = other.clone()`, and only `put` clears extras. Replace an array formula's anchor through `cell_mut` with a plain number and the writer emits `<c r="B2"><f t="array" ref="B2:B4"/><v>5</v></c>`. The empty-text array `<f>` is a formula Excel repairs. `inline_runs` and `shared_string` are guarded by a text-equality check, but this fact is not.
findings.fix: In `PartWriter::cell`, honour `FormulaKind::Array` attributes (and `cm`, which is already gated on it) only when `cell.formula().is_some()`. Add a pin: `cell_mut`, assign a number over an array anchor, save, and assert no `t="array"` in the part.

findings.issue: `Layout::insert_rows` and `remove_rows` move the row formats, but the modelled merged ranges (and the frozen pane) are left where they were. A sheet that read `<mergeCells>` and then takes `Sheet::insert_rows` or `remove_rows` writes the merges at their old rows next to cells that moved. Merges are a model fact of this phase, not a carried one, so the shift belongs here. The carried elements' shifting is P4 by plan.
findings.fix: Shift merges in `insert_rows` (a merge spanning the insertion point grows, one below moves down) and shrink or drop them in `remove_rows`, or refuse the edit while `merges` is non-empty until P4 moves the verbs to `Workbook`. Add a pin in rust/tests/excel/layout.rs beside `a_row_format_moves_with_the_rows_below_an_insertion...`.

findings.issue: Two costs of the shared-strings write are unpinned, against the AGENTS cost rule. (a) A save that appends a string reads the original sst member a second time (workbook.rs:1584 `self.source.read(held)`) after `strings()` already parsed it. The `iobase_calls` excel pins only save numbers, so this extra read appears in no count. (b) `rewrite` now clones (`into_owned`) and decodes (`text_piece`) every text, CDATA and reference event for every caller, including the rewrite of a whole sst, even though only `definedName` uses the `text` hook. That is an allocation per `<t>` of a large table.
findings.fix: Add an `iobase_calls` row for a save that appends one string, stating the sst read count. Make the `text` hook an `Option` (or gate on a flag) so `rewrite` buffers text events only when a hook was given, and pin the sst rewrite in the allocations excel rows at two table sizes.

findings.issue: Design 12.3 direction B says Rust edits one cell per sheet. The fidelity half edits two cells of `Data` only and never touches `Report`, which stays a raw copy. The written-again formula path for a cross-sheet reference (`=Rate*Data!C2`, `=SUM(Data!C2:C5)`) is therefore never exercised against openpyxl, and its assertions are trivially true.
findings.fix: In `edits_one_cell_of_the_workbook_the_external_writer_filled_with_every_feature` (rust/tests/interop/excel.rs), also `set_cell` on `Report` (for example A3), so `Report` is written again from its cells. In `read_fidelity_with_openpyxl`, keep the `Report!A1` and `Report!A2` formula and defined-name assertions and add the new cell.

findings.issue: Lexer::qualified slices `self.rest(at)[..5]` at a byte offset that can fall inside a multibyte char, so `Formula::from_file` (documented as total) panics. It is hit whenever a sheet-qualified name starts with non-ASCII letters that are not a cell reference: `Sheet1!Größe`, `Лист1!Итого`, `Sheet1!名前`. Verified against the real crate: `Workbook::from_bytes` panics at open on a defined name `Sheet1!Итого`, and `Workbook::sheet` panics on a cell `<f>Sheet1!Größe*2</f>`. `Formula::from_entry` reaches the same slice. A 300k-string fuzz of the lexer found this as the only panic site; a 4k-iteration mutation run over the rich package found no other.
findings.fix: Use a boundary-safe compare: `if self.rest(at).get(..5).is_some_and(|head| head.eq_ignore_ascii_case("#REF!")) {`. Add pins in rust/tests/excel/formula/lexer.rs and a Workbook-open test for `Sheet1!Größe`, `Лист1!Итого`, `Sheet1!名前` as a cell formula and as a defined name.

findings.issue: `Sheet::hold_in` for a sheet from another workbook resets cell, row and column styles, but the carried `conditionalFormatting` keeps every `cfRule dxfId`. That index points into the source workbook's `dxfs`. Verified: a `Data` sheet from rich_package() inserted into `Workbook::new()` writes `<cfRule type="cellIs" dxfId="0" ...>` while the target styles.xml has no `<dxfs>`, so the reference dangles. Excel repairs the file. Where the target does have dxfs, it silently applies another workbook's differential format. The test a_sheet_moved_to_another_workbook_... asserts `<conditionalFormatting` is kept without checking this.
findings.fix: In the foreign-origin branch of `hold_in` (or in `WorksheetFrame::detach`), rewrite the carried `conditionalFormatting` items with `package::rewrite` and `attributes: |name| if name == b"cfRule" { vec![("dxfId", None)] } else { vec![] }`. Colour scales, data bars and icon sets need no dxf. Alternatively intern the source dxf into the target styles. Extend the test to assert no `dxfId` survives.

findings.issue: `insert_sheet` replacing a same-named tab builds the slot with `slot_of`, which takes a fresh `SheetKey`. `DefinedName::scope` still holds the old key. While `names_touched` is false the names are copied verbatim and keep `localSheetId`. After any earlier rename, remove or move has set `names_touched`, `workbook_document` resolves the old key to no tab and `DefinedName::element(None)` removes `localSheetId`. Verified with the rich package: `rename_sheet("Report","Rep")` then `insert_sheet(Data)` writes `_xlnm._FilterDatabase` as a workbook-global hidden name instead of scoped to `Data`. Scoped built-in names silently become global.
findings.fix: Do not reuse the old key, because a stale in-flight Package snapshot must not mark the new sheet saved. In the replace branch, re-scope every name with `scope() == Some(old_key)` to the new key (add a crate-private `DefinedName::set_scope`, leaving `read.1` untouched so the raw element is still reused), or drop those names as `remove_sheet` does. Pin: rename, replace, save, and the name keeps `localSheetId`.

findings.issue: In `word()`, `first:last!ref` is read as a 3D sheet span whenever both sides are word characters, even when `first` reads as a reference. `A1:Sheet1!A1`, `C:C:Sheet1!1:1` and `R1C1:Sheet1!A:A` lex as a span of sheets `A1`..`Sheet1` and render as `'A1:Sheet1'!A1`. That is a different formula, written back on every dirty save. Excel requires quotes for reference-like sheet names, so an unquoted span cannot start that way. Found by a canonical-text round-trip fuzz; every other canonical input round-trips exactly.
findings.fix: Take the unquoted `Some(':')` span branch only when `self.target_at(start).is_none()`, so `A1:Sheet1!A1` falls through to reference, `:`, reference. `Jan:Mar!B2` still lexes as a span. Add a round-trip pin for `A1:Sheet1!A1` and `A:A:Sheet1!1:1`.

findings.issue: `WorksheetFrame::detach` drops a whole carried child if any of its text names a relationship prefix. `<pageSetup ... r:id="rId1"/>` (printerSettings, on most Windows-saved sheets) loses paperSize, orientation, scale and fitToPage. `<hyperlinks>` loses its in-workbook `location` links whenever one link uses `r:id`. Excel keeps page setup when a sheet moves between workbooks. The test a_sheet_moved_to_another_workbook_... asserts `<pageSetup` is gone, so it pins the loss.
findings.fix: Detach at attribute or child granularity. Strip only the `r:id` attribute from `pageSetup` (and any Free element), and drop only `<hyperlink>` children carrying `r:id`, using `package::rewrite` with `skip`/`attributes` on the carried bytes. Drop the whole element only when nothing is left (`drawing`, `legacyDrawing`, `tableParts`, `picture`). Update the test to expect `pageSetup` kept without `r:id` and internal hyperlinks kept.

findings.issue: When a sheet is removed, only the `[Content_Types]` Overrides of the dropped parts themselves are removed. LibreOffice writes `<Override PartName="/xl/worksheets/_rels/sheet1.xml.rels" .../>`. The `.rels` member is skipped in the copy loop, but its Override stays. Verified by removing `Data` from a LibreOffice-written workbook: the output has a dangling Override for `/xl/worksheets/_rels/sheet1.xml.rels`.
findings.fix: In `content_types_document`, build `dropped` from each dropped part plus `package::relationships_part_of(part)`, matching the member-skip condition in `write_preserving`. Pin with a content-types fixture that has an Override for a dropped part's `.rels`.

findings.issue: `set_cell` builds a fresh default-style cell (`put` also drops the extras), so overwriting a percent-, currency- or fill-styled cell silently resets its style. The pins a_sheet_written_again_keeps_every_byte_outside_its_cells and an_edited_cell_changes_only_its_cell encode this (`<c r="B2" s="2">` becomes `<c r="B2">`). The interop edits only unstyled cells, so nothing checks it. This existed before P2 but P2's fidelity claim ('changes only its cell') now rests on it.
findings.fix: Either state in the pins and docs that a value write resets the cell's style, with typed entry in P3 as the styled-edit door, or make `set_cell` carry over the replaced cell's `StyleId` (except when a temporal value picks its own) and add a styled cell to the openpyxl fidelity half.

fixed.summary:
I checked all 15 findings against the code. Every one was real, and each is fixed and has a pin. Several were reported twice under different severities.

1. **Lexer panic on non-ASCII text after a sheet prefix (the blocker and the major).** `Lexer::qualified` now reads the `#REF!` head with `rest(at).get(..5).is_some_and(..)`, so it no longer cuts a character in half. Pins: `Sheet1!Größe`, `'Q1'!Größe*2`, `Sheet1!abcdé`, `Лист1!Итого`, `Sheet1!名前` in `every_byte_of_any_text_is_kept`, plus a new `from_file`/`from_entry` pin. A new names test opens a workbook holding these as cell formulas and as defined names, renames the sheet, saves, and checks the text.
2. **`cargo doc` warnings.** The formula.rs and layout.rs links are now plain text, and the two sheet.rs links are bare. `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p yggdryl --no-deps` is clean.
3. **Conditional-format `dxfId` kept on a sheet moved to another workbook (both reports).** A new `WorksheetFrame::forget_styles` removes every `dxfId` attribute from the carried children. `Sheet::hold_in` calls it only when the sheet comes from another workbook. A rule keeps its condition and loses its format, the same way a cell falls back to the default style. The 2010 (x14) conditional formats keep theirs, because they carry the format inline. The move pin now expects the rule with no `dxfId`. A new pin shows a sheet removed and put back in its own workbook keeps `dxfId="0"`.
4. **`detach` dropped whole children over a text match (both reports).** It now parses each carried child and finds relationship attributes by the prefixes the root and the child bind to the relationships namespace. That catches a tab or newline before `r:id`, and any prefix name.
   - `pageSetup` loses only its `r:id`.
   - `hyperlinks` and `extLst` lose only the children that name a relationship.
   - Anything else that names one (`drawing`, `legacyDrawing`, `tableParts`, …) goes whole.
   The pin expects `<pageSetup paperSize="9" orientation="landscape"/>` and the `location` hyperlink to survive. A new pin covers a custom prefix, tab and newline spacing, and an `ext` that declares the namespace itself.
5. **Stale pivot-cache list across saves.** The `Stated::pivot_caches` field is deleted. Whether `<pivotCaches>` is dropped is now decided by counting the cache entries in the workbook part as it is stored, which a previous save rewrote. New pin: a package with two caches, saved twice, once through `write_into` and once through `rebase`.
6. **Array attributes written on a cell that no longer holds a formula.** `PartWriter::cell` now ignores array attributes, and the `cm` that goes with them, when the cell has no formula. Data-table attributes are kept, since a data table's `<f>` has no text. Two pins: a number put over an array anchor through `cell_mut`, and an anchor still holding its formula.
7. **Merges and the frozen split did not move with rows.** `Layout::insert_rows` and `remove_rows` now move them the way Excel does:
   - Inserting: a merge below the insertion point moves down, and one spanning it grows. Inserting inside the frozen rows moves the split down.
   - Removing: a merge inside the removed rows goes, one across them shrinks, and one left as a single cell is dropped. The split loses the frozen rows removed and goes when nothing is left frozen.
   A new `Layout::stands_from` stops the sheet's early return from skipping a sheet that has merges but no cells. New pin in the layout tests.
8. **Shared-strings costs.**
   - (a) A new `iobase_calls` row covers a save that appends a string. The table is read once in place of being copied, so the call count is the same as a plain save (10); the extra cost is the inflate, and the comment says so.
   - (b) The `Rewrite::text` hook is now an `Option`, so text is buffered only when a hook is given. `rewrite` no longer allocates per element: `Opened` holds an inline `SmolStr`, and `patch_start` borrows a start tag it does not edit.
   - New allocations pin: extending a table of 64 and of 4,096 strings both cost 197 allocations.
9. **The openpyxl fidelity check never rewrote `Report`.** The Rust half now also edits `Report!A3`, so that sheet is written again from its cells, and checks its formulas after reopening. The Python half asserts `Report!A3`. The exchange passes with no SKIPPED.
10. **Replacing a same-named sheet lost the scope of its names.** `insert_sheet` now moves every name scoped to the old key onto the new sheet, through a crate-private `DefinedName::set_scope`. Pin: rename a sheet, replace another, save, and `localSheetId="0"` is kept.
11. **`A1:Sheet1!A1` read as a span of sheets.** An unquoted `first:last!` is now a span only when neither side is a name Excel would have to quote (the renderer's `needs_quotes`). Round-trip pins for `A1:Sheet1!A1`, `C:C:Sheet1!1:1`, `R1C1:Sheet1!A:A` and `Sheet1!A1:Sheet1!B2`; `Jan:Mar!B2` still reads as a span.
12. **A dropped part's `.rels` Override stayed in `[Content_Types]`.** The Overrides removed now include each dropped part's relationships part. Pin uses a content-types part that states Overrides for relationships parts, as the finding reports LibreOffice doing.
13. **`set_cell` resets the cell's style.** Not changed; documented instead (see deviations). `Sheet::set_cell` now says the new cell takes the default style and shows, in a runnable doc example, how to keep it with `Cell::with_style` and `insert_cell`. The pin comment in the carried tests says the same.

No public name was added or removed.

deviations: set_cell style finding: I took the finding's first option (state the reset in the docs and pins) rather than carrying the replaced cell's StyleId over. set_cell is the low-level value door that from_serie and write_serie are built on, and the design makes P3's Workbook::set_entry the styled, Excel-like entry door. The set_cell rustdoc now states the reset and shows how to keep a style through Cell::with_style and insert_cell.

Foreign conditional formats: the dxfId attribute is removed from every carried element that states one (cfRule, and also colorFilter or sortCondition if present, where the schema makes it optional). The finding's alternative was to hold the element until P3 can intern and remap dxfs; stripping the index was chosen for now, and P3 can replace it with a remap.

Shared-strings read on save: the table is still read a second time (the parse keeps items, not bytes). The iobase_calls pin shows this read takes the place of the copy the member would otherwise get, so the call count is the same as a plain save; the extra cost is the inflate. The raw bytes were not kept in memory to avoid it.

Moving rows now also moves the frozen split: Layout::insert_rows moves it down when rows are inserted inside the frozen rows, and remove_rows shrinks it. The finding named the pane without saying how it should move; this is my understanding of Excel's behaviour.

Sheet::insert_rows and remove_rows still leave the carried Shifted elements (conditionalFormatting, dataValidations, autoFilter, hyperlinks and the rest) at their old rows, and do not refuse the edit when a Blocking element is present.
